title: The universe in a single day
caption: The Big Bang at midnight, today at the next midnight.

annotations.text: Invention of writing: 23:59:59, less than a second before midnight

scaleNote: Each second on this clock is about 159,722 years.

events.label: Big Bang
events.description: The universe begins hot and dense and starts expanding.

events.label: First stars and galaxies
events.description: The first stars ignite within a few hundred million years of the Big Bang.
events.source: Estimate from JWST and Hubble deep-field observations (NASA); timing still debated

events.label: Sun and Solar System form
events.description: A collapsing gas cloud forms the Sun and its disk of planets.
events.source: Meteorite (CAI) radiometric ages, e.g. Connelly et al. 2012, Science

events.label: Earth forms
events.description: Earth assembles from colliding rocky bodies.
events.source: US Geological Survey, age of the Earth

events.label: Earliest evidence of life
events.description: Earliest traces of microbial life in ancient rocks.
events.source: Peer-reviewed fossil and isotope evidence (e.g. Nutman et al. 2016, Nature); still debated

events.label: Great Oxidation Event
events.description: Microbes start filling the atmosphere with oxygen.
events.source: Geological record of atmospheric oxygen (peer-reviewed estimate)

events.label: Cambrian explosion of animal life
events.description: Complex animals appear rapidly in the fossil record.
events.source: International Commission on Stratigraphy, base of the Cambrian

events.label: Non-bird dinosaurs die out
events.description: An asteroid impact ends the age of dinosaurs.
events.source: International Commission on Stratigraphy, end of the Cretaceous

events.label: First Homo sapiens
events.description: The oldest known fossils of our species.
events.source: Jebel Irhoud fossils, Hublin et al. 2017, Nature

events.label: Invention of writing
events.before: less than a second before midnight
